title: Effects of Adaptive Servo-Ventilation in Heart Failure Patients with preserved Ejection Fraction and Central Sleep Apnea on Nocturnal Blood Pressure (VENT-HF I Blood Pressure) – A Multicenter Randomized Cross-Over Withdrawal Study
summary:
Background
Many people with a form of heart failure in which the pumping function of the heart is still largely preserved also experience disturbances of breathing during sleep. These breathing pauses can disturb sleep and may be associated with elevated blood pressure. Treatment often includes nighttime breathing support using a device and mask that helps stabilize breathing. However, it is not yet well understood how this treatment affects nighttime blood pressure.

Research question
The study investigates whether nighttime blood pressure changes when nighttime breathing support is temporarily paused. It will also examine whether sleep quality, symptoms, and quality of life change during this period.

Methods
About 110 adult participants from several clinics will take part in the study. All participants already use nighttime breathing support. During the study, this treatment will either be continued or temporarily paused for a short period of time. In both phases, blood pressure, sleep, symptoms, and quality of life will be measured and compared.

interventions.name:
ASV OFF-to-ON arm: During Intervention Phase I (two weeks),  ASV therapy will be discontinued. Following a two-week washout period, Intervention Phase II (two weeks) will start, during which ASV therapy will be resumed.

Abbreviation: adaptive servo-ventilation = ASV

ASV ON-to-OFF arm: During Intervention Phase I (two weeks),  ASV therapy will be continued. Following a two-week washout period, Intervention Phase II (two weeks) will start, during which ASV therapy will be withdrawn.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Established therapy with ASV prescribed in clinical routine for >6 months and mean daily use ≥4h per night
- Stable HFpEF defined as: signs and/or symptoms of heart failure, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥40%, and objective evidence of cardiac structural and/or functional abnormalities consistent with elevated left ventricular filling pressures, defined as either (1) elevated natriuretic peptide levels (NT-proBNP >125 pg/mL in sinus rhythm or >365 pg/mL in atrial fibrillation, or BNP >35 pg/mL in sinus rhythm or >105 pg/mL in atrial fibrillation) and at least one echocardiographic criterion, or (2) normal natriuretic peptide levels and at least two echocardiographic criteria. Echocardiographic criteria are: left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial dilatation, elevated E/e′ at rest, and elevated estimated systolic pulmonary artery pressure or tricuspid regurgitation velocity
- systolic BP <180 mmHg and diastolic BP <110 mmHg
- Adherence to stable antihypertensive and heart failure medication (≥4 weeks prior to randomization), diuretics and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, if prescribed
- Written informed consent (VENT-HF Observation and VENT-HF Blood Pressure)
Exclusion criteria:
- History of any sleep related accident or current professional drivers
- Known non-tolerance of ASV withdrawal
- Drug induced CSA (e.g., opioids)
- Non-cardiac causes for heart failure-like symptoms (pulmonary disease, obesity with body-mass index >45 kg/m², anemia (Hb<10 g/dl))
- Secondary hypertension (other than sleep-disordered breathing)
- Severe valvular heart disease
- Severe pulmonary disease
- Any other medical, social, or geographical factor that would make it unlikely that the patient will comply with the study procedures
- Participation in concurrent placebo controlled studies in which a change in therapy occurs during participation in the VENT-HF I Blood Pressure study
